title: High-gamma dataset described in Schirrmeister et al. 2017
description: A high-gamma EEG dataset comprising 14 healthy subjects performing motor imagery tasks (left hand, right hand, feet, and rest) recorded at 500 Hz with 128 channels. This derivative dataset was used to develop and validate deep convolutional neural networks for end-to-end EEG decoding, demonstrating that deep learning approaches can match or exceed traditional feature-based methods (FBCSP) while learning interpretable spectral power modulations in alpha, beta, and high-gamma frequency bands.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired at 500 Hz sampling rate using 128 channels arranged in the standard 1005 montage. Subjects performed four motor imagery tasks (left hand sequential finger-tapping, right hand sequential finger-tapping, feet toe clenching, and rest) cued by visual arrows. Each session contained 2 runs with 13 blocks per run, totaling 80 trials per run (4-second trial duration, 3-4 second inter-trial intervals). Deep learning models (shallow ConvNets, deep ConvNets, ResNets) were compared against FBCSP baseline using within-subject holdout cross-validation with cropped training strategies.
